text: Purpose and Scope of the Document

This document presents the requirements, architecture, design, development process, testing, deployment, and maintenance plan for WashWise. It guides the development and evaluation of a mobile application for laundry ordering, branch selection, processing visibility, ready notifications, and in-person settlement. Customers, staff, and administrators have separate responsibilities under the updated project workflow.

The intended audience consists of the project adviser and evaluators, the student development team, laundry shop administrators and staff, and customer representatives. Technical sections guide implementation, while the requirements and workflow explain the expected behavior to users.

The proposed WashWise mobile application will provide customers with a convenient way to create laundry orders, select between Regular and Rush/Express services, view an estimated price, and monitor the progress of their laundry. After submitting an order, customers will personally bring their dirty laundry to the laundry shop, where staff will verify the actual laundry and determine the final price. When the laundry is ready and the customer returns to collect it, the customer will pay the laundry shop in person. The system will not process online payments or provide delivery services. Instead, laundry staff will manage the processing schedule based on the selected service and current workload, while customers can monitor the status of their laundry through the application.

The updated workflow distinguishes customer self-registration from staff provisioning. Only the administrator creates staff accounts, using an email address and temporary password through a protected backend. Ready notification precedes payment and collection. An order becomes completed only after staff record the payment and confirm pickup.

text: In the project title, pickup means the customer collects finished laundry at the selected shop. Scheduling refers to staff-managed processing order and Regular or Rush/Express priority. It does not mean laundry delivery or customer-controlled collection reservations.
Administrator: Laundry shop administrator authorized to manage staff access, branches, and pricing.
User Registration/Login - Allows customers to register and securely access their accounts. Staff and administrators log in using authorized accounts; staff cannot register themselves.

Staff/Admin Management - Allows staff to manage assigned branch orders, processing priorities, payments, and laundry statuses. The administrator manages staff accounts, branches, and prices and monitors operational records.

Authentication and live data updates require an internet connection. Push notifications depend on device permission and delivery services, so the application also retains an in-app notification and the current order status. Estimates are advisory and may change with verified laundry details and branch workload.

rows: FR01
Customers register, log in, recover access, and maintain their own profiles. Registration cannot grant staff or administrator privileges.
FR02
Customers browse branch details, prices, and locations, select a branch, and open map directions.
FR03
Customers choose service and Regular or Rush/Express priority, enter laundry details, and confirm an estimate. Submission creates an owned order with pending_dropoff status.
FR04
Authorized branch staff inspect the laundry, verify actual weight or items, confirm the final price, and change the order to received.
FR05
Staff update received to washing to drying to ready; customers can view only their own order progress.
FR06
The ready transition creates a customer notification and initiates a push alert before payment and collection.
FR07
Staff verify the in-person payment against the final amount and confirm collection before setting completed.
FR08
Customers view their own completed history; staff view authorized branch records; administrators monitor operational records.
FR09
Only an administrator creates staff using email and temporary password. The backend sets role=staff, createdBy, createdAt, and isActive=true.
FR10
Administrators deactivate/reactivate staff and manage branches and prices. Deactivation preserves the account and audit records.
FR11
Authorized cancellation records cancelled status and an optional reason under the shop-approved policy without erasing payment or history.
FR12
Orders, payments, notifications, and account administration retain ownership, branch, actor, and timestamp information for traceability.

text: The following are proposed acceptance targets to be measured during testing, rather than results already achieved.

rows: Performance

Common reads complete within 3 seconds in at least 95% of 30 trials on the agreed device and stable network; a confirmed status change appears in a second connected session within 5 seconds. Record test conditions.
Security

Deny cross-customer access, unauthorized branch updates, role escalation, and customer payment edits. Require active staff/admin authorization for privileged operations. Passwords remain only in Firebase Authentication.
Usability
Use clear labels, consistent navigation, readable forms, and visible validation. Representative users complete their assigned core scenario without a critical error; record assistance needed.
Reliability
Retries do not create duplicate orders, payments, or ready notifications. Failed requests never display false success, and pending saves do not overwrite the last confirmed state.
Data integrity
Validate quantities, branch ownership, monetary values, and state transitions. Use server timestamps and preserve the pricing basis used by an order.
Compatibility
Evaluate customer and operational screens on selected Android devices. Additional platform releases require separate configuration and verification.
Maintainability
Separate screens, service logic, and data access. Use readable TypeScript types, reviewed changes, versioned rules, and repeatable tests.
Recovery
Back up operational data before risky changes and verify restoration in staging. Reconcile orders and payments before reopening affected writes.

text: WashWise uses a client and cloud-service architecture. Customer screens handle registration, branches, ordering, tracking, alerts, and history. Staff screens handle the branch queue, intake verification, processing, and payment recording. Administrator screens handle staff access, branches, prices, and monitoring. These are logical role-based interfaces; the workflow does not require three separately deployed applications.

Firebase Authentication establishes identity, and Cloud Firestore stores customer and operational records. Security rules constrain permitted client data access. Trusted backend functions handle privileged actions and validate identity, role, active status, ownership, branch access, and allowed transitions. Hiding a screen is not an authorization control.
